review.description: S3/S4 provide one owned local invocation that reconciles reviewed specifications and verifies the branch while sharing only identical required command vectors in the same directory and stable environment. Reuse binds source, prepared artifacts, helper/toolchain selection, comparison and review decisions throughout the invocation. Source watches begin before initial analysis and native planning. Restored hard-link or mapped writes, existing writers, uncertain admission and lost monitoring coverage reject. Administrator/kernel trust and unsupported lease/signal contexts are explicit. Product-flow adoption, foundational meanings and outstanding real-host gaps remain unchanged. Input admission timing distinguishes preplanning source/review/planner inputs, pre-preparation external dependencies and post-preparation artifacts. Nonempty Python import selectors require absolute paths so root and browser-helper working directories cannot select unbound external roots. S3/S4 also preserve the ordinary reconciliation route with bounded deadlines for only the two exact maintained root suites and require native admission to include extensions beneath nested package directory aliases. S3/S4 isolate retained Go compilation caches and start each required command with empty private cache state; the pinned selected headless executable receives native admission. Command-result sharing remains guarded, while compilation across different required commands starts fresh and adds overhead. Checkout pathname ancestry is now bound before initial watched traversal. Authored S3/S4 prose explicitly covers restored ancestor substitution with original root and Makefile inodes preserved; glossary/UI ownership and pinned product adoption remain unchanged.
review.implementation: Inspected the native Make planner, invocation executor and reconciliation callback. Exact preparation first occurrences remain owned in one environment; required suites share guarded executions and retain attempted durations on failure. Typed nonblocking regular-file descriptors bind source snapshots, artifacts, review bytes, cache entries and file-based discovery without FIFO blocking; reconciliation consumes admitted immutable decision bytes. Helper discovery/candidate watches share npm working contexts and prefixes, retain alias closure and include executable interpreters, native libraries, compiler resources, Go/Python dependencies, browser installations and Git revision/status inputs including private worktree refs. Fresh watched checked-hash bytecode excludes only unused automatic outputs; importable nested sources and legacy bytecode remain inputs. Inode/directory watches and shared per-inode read leases reject existing writers/mappings and persistently invalidate before later writers proceed. Observed monitor errors remain invalid after draining. Root-owned nonwritable maintained local-filesystem tools retain metadata/inode checks under explicit administrator trust. Signal-blocked registry updates, fork-aware ownership and checked disposal restore caller state. Failed execution or late teardown invalidates exact owned publications while preserving primary cancellation and subsequent atomic replacements. Duplicate descriptors close before owner registration; secondary close errors preserve the original admission failure. Planning-source monitoring installs the selected Make executable and all PATH-candidate watches before native plan capture. Python import-root selectors reject relative and empty entries before ownership and before discovery subprocesses; absolute and unset selectors preserve ordinary behavior. Production code is unchanged by the hosted-fixture repair: local-only admission, read-lease trust and native search boundaries remain intact. Fixture setup isolates caller host markers and unrelated fallback launcher directories, and the explicit real ABI control selects the maintained distro Python. Ordinary reconciliation and the combined coordinator share one exact long-suite argv set; ordinary dispatch supplies 900 seconds only to its default runner for those vectors and leaves custom executors in control. Native admission expands helper_roots before scanning ELF modules, retaining those aliases for subsequent identity and mutation monitoring. CI guide and authored flow now explain the actual order and ordinary deadline policy. GoCache binds the authenticated-owner private directory and empties cache output before each required command, excluding retained and previous-command compilation archives from later checks without freezing Go mutable index records. Directory selection/lookup/inode guards survive summary publication; checked disposal precedes owner teardown and restores caller selection. Native admission includes chrome-headless-shell. Public entrypoint bootstrap now validates the same supported Python-selector policy before application imports, using bootstrap os/sys only. Direct library API admission remains independently enforced. Test-supervisor readiness is an explicit bounded pipe protocol before its inner deadline; cleanup behavior is unchanged. The real-ABI test now supplies an explicit minimal inventory containing a byte-identical distro libc copy selected from actual ldconfig output, while retaining the actual system loader, native tools and cache metadata. Production discovery and fail-closed ELF search policy are unchanged. Inspected InputWatch.__init__: existing external(root, contents=False) installs name-filtered ancestor-resolution watches before pending tree traversal, using the established watch/lease cleanup on exceptions. Initial planning_source therefore binds the lexical checkout path before native Make reads, rather than relying on later Session admission. Existing Session/Go-cache revalidation and sibling-name filtering remain.
review.tests: Reviewed actual assertions for native-plan fidelity, exact sharing, independent Go race runs, changed source/artifacts/helpers/environment/comparison, malformed decisions, stale evidence and failure/cancellation through publication and teardown. Supervised FIFO/descriptor matrices require prompt rejection, closed descriptors, original SIGINT/SIGTERM outcomes, no successful outputs and released ownership. Temporary Make plans, actual launcher/interpreter execution, npm config, compiler headers, Go VCS/private refs and nested Python source/legacy imports exercise consumed changed inputs before restoration. The hard-link regression records temporary source consumed by a required subprocess, then requires rejection after exact restoration and reacquires ownership. Prefaulted shared mappings reject admission on checkout storage and tmpfs after writable descriptors close, before native planning. A later shared mapping consumes changed bytes and restores them while both writer and mapping remain open; success still rejects. Readonly/private-copy mappings and overlapping aliases retain supported behavior. Fork-child disposal preserves the parent lease. Lost/forced leases, unsupported admission, occupied/blocked SIGIO, queued teardown breaks, actual close failure and acquisition SIGINT assert conservative rejection plus descriptor/signal restoration. The overflow control requires later unchanged-input checks to remain invalid after failed evidence was drained. A failed duplicate close leaves exactly one existing owner and a valid parent lease, then final disposal releases all references. Unsupported admission remains the primary failure when actual descriptor closure also reports an error. The external Make-shadow control runs a real wrapper that filters the native vet recipe then removes itself; it records the incomplete captured graph and requires rejection before runner execution or receipts, while genuine Make includes vet. The Python-context control observes different actual external roots under root versus browser cwd and a zero-exit imported module that skips the required body. Relative/empty PYTHONPATH and relative PYTHONHOME/PYTHONUSERBASE reject before ownership, planning or discovery; absolute and empty selectors complete an invocation. Rechecked the unchanged subject-specific assertions and current shared suite input after the fixture portability repair: local-verification fixtures now clear inherited GITHUB_ACTIONS, retain only selected installation and distro helper search directories, and the real native ABI control selects distro Python. The explicit hosted-marker rejection test asserts no required command or receipt, while the full fixture suite is separately exercised under an inherited hosted marker. These test-context corrections do not change this subject contract or waive production input admission. The C-library mutation/negative controls now inventory their explicit compiled fixtures rather than unrelated host launchers. An actual Python-name ELF with a private RUNPATH reproduced three false early rejections before the correction; afterward all real load/mutation and own-input negative assertions complete successfully. Current ordinary-reconciliation deadline and native-alias correction: inspected actual exact-vector/custom-executor dispatch and timeout invalidation assertions, plus Python-loaded header-free native library import through two directory aliases. The control consumes value 7; unsupported private RUNPATH rejects before any required command or receipt. Explicitly inventoried dependencies consuming value 9 and restoring bytes invalidate evidence. These operational assertions refresh this subject suite without changing product semantics or closing real-host gaps. The native-alias fixture now uses a Python package loading a plain C library through ctypes; every C fixture compiles with -nostdinc and no Python C API/include-directory lookup. Its real package import, value7 control, pre-run outside-RUNPATH rejection and consumed/restored value9 assertions remain intact. The same real test passes when an outer compiler probe disables all headers and strips explicit include paths; the former Python.h fixture fails in that context. This removes an undeclared test prerequisite without changing production admission or this subject behavior. Current cache/browser controls exercise actual same-size Go archive tampering with an unchanged build ID, showing value9 under the prior production implementation for both environment and GOENV selectors. Independent new invocations ignore those external archives and consume7. Earlier-command cache entries are removed before a subsequent check; changing their retained hard-link alias to9 still yields7 from fresh compilation. Caller environment and cache disposal are asserted. Late cache-directory binding changes and disposal failures invalidate successful publications while preserving original failures/cancellation. Pinned chrome-headless-shell and its older spelling reject real outside-RUNPATH/alternate-interpreter ELF controls before runner calls or receipts. These operational assertions add no product or real-host acceptance. The probe supervisor now records cancellation rather than throwing across child assignment or cleanup entry. A deterministic SIGINT at its first cleanup instruction preserves exit130 and reaps both a TERM-ignoring child and detached grandchild, with an outer supervisor protecting failure cleanup. The prior supervisor was directly observed leaving two descendants alive under that exact schedule; this closes that specific test-helper gap only. The scheduling microbenchmark fixture now initializes the optional Go cache field when deliberately bypassing Session construction; actual assertions still require27 preparation entries,8 executions,35 versus16 scans, ordered contexts and environment-change rejection. Current public-CLI/bootstrap and probe-readiness correction: the actual entrypoint previously consumed a relative secrets.py and exited0 before verification (retained direct before control). New subprocess assertions require nonzero rejection before module consumption, while direct API and admitted-root controls remain. The cleanup probe receives a pipe acknowledgement after its child and detached grandchild PID marker exists before starting its inner deadline; first-cleanup SIGINT, exit130, no survivors and outer cleanup assertions remain. The real Go VCS-stamping fixture now retains build stdout/stderr on failure; original and alternate embedded revisions, restored source and failed-receipt assertions remain intact. An old-head independent Make failed that build with captured stderr omitted, while its isolated diagnostic and the corrected focused fixture pass. No root cause or flaky-test exception is claimed; a new independent Make remains mandatory before merge. The real system loader --list resolves the compiled header-free probe to that copied libc, and the probe executes successfully. Real readelf discovery includes loader, cache and copied libc. A separately compiled cached ELF with an existing unrepresented RUNPATH must still reject; unsupported loader environment controls remain. An outer cache-contamination control injects an actual unrelated custom-RUNPATH library into real ldconfig output: the former positive control rejects, and the isolated positive plus explicit negative controls pass. This scopes fixture prerequisites without accepting the unrelated library or weakening production admission. Added test_planning_rejects_restored_checkout_ancestor_substitution with actual native Make and review/tools/tmp outside the moved ancestor. Planning and initial-watch-construction schedules preserve original checkout/Makefile inodes and final source bytes. Direct old implementation returned verified:true for both schedules with no vet command and reconciled receipts. Corrected implementation rejects both before runner calls/receipts; actual focused eight-method run passed17.275s. The genuine native graph contains vet, and existing restored-Makefile, removed-planner-shadow, lease alias, cache and descriptor controls passed. Full ordinary432-test reconciliation and separate committed-head Make remain required; focused evidence alone grants no final acceptance.
